newsitem.title: POLAND: Universal mulls Hyundai car plant.
newsitem.headline: Universal mulls Hyundai car plant.

text.p: The joint venture between Polish trading firm Universal and South Korea's Hyundai Corp is considering building a car factory in Poland to expand its current car assembly plant, a Universal spokesman said on Thursday.

Krzysztof Bien told Reuters the company would build a manufacturing facility if the government refused to grant it a licence to import car parts duty free for its assembly plant in Pultusk, central Poland.
"If not granted the permit, we will build a factory in Pultusk," he said, adding the company would also take the government to court if it were denied the licence.
The factory, in which most parts for production would have to be domestically made, would be automatically exempted from customs duty, now between six and 35 percent.
Bien suggested such a factory could produce about 100,000 cars annually.

The foreign trade ministry is expected to decide on the permit by the end of the month. Earlier the industry ministry recommended it to deny the permission, saying the Pultusk factory did not fulfil requirements of an assembly plant.
Bien declined to disclose how the new investment would be financed but he did not rule out that part of it could be financed by Hyundai.
Earlier this year, Hyundai said it was considering investing about $1 billion in Poland within the next several years.
